hypothesis: Buying active common stocks at the next session open after an official conventional forward stock-split execution date, with pre-event liquidity floors and a fixed ten-session hold, produces after-cost replacement value above the same-date cash-feasible core candidate when one exists and cash otherwise, because a conventional forward split is a deliberate board-approved corporate action correlated with management confidence, nominal-price accessibility and attention, and the research-PIT month-start Massive membership (future revisions quarantined) keeps later-delisted issuers in the sample, which the current-roster warehouse cannot represent.

provenance.baseline_policy: same-decision-date cash-feasible core candidate if present, otherwise cash

independent_evidence.decision_exclusions: descriptive fields, FIGIs, current reference rows and future vendor revisions

expectation_gap.gap_definition: The cash-feasible core-or-cash prior prices the best currently admitted opportunity as the slot hurdle; the official forward-split execution event is an independent, exchange-public corporate action whose medium-horizon drift the core candidate pool cannot represent because most splitting issuers are outside the core roster.

transmission.catalyst: Forward split execution: a board-approved action correlated with management confidence, plus nominal-price accessibility, retail attention and improved optionability known at the execution-date close.
transmission.expected_direction: Selected post-split names should exceed the return of the displaced core candidate or cash over the identical costed ten-session interval.
transmission.half_life: Next session open through the tenth subsequent trading session.

why_not_arbitraged: Conventional common-stock forward splits are scarce (roughly eight liquid events per six-month window after event-purity filtering), the modern post-split drift literature is mixed and mostly announcement-anchored, round-trip costs and a scarce cash-funded slot must be paid, and smaller splitting names carry reversal and concentration risk.
falsifier: Reject unless every standard window has at least five selected touches under the frozen conventional-ratio predicate and strictly positive after-cost replacement value, aggregate replacement value is strictly positive, the double-cost aggregate remains positive, the maximum single-ticker positive contribution is at most 50%, the top-five share is at most 60%, contribution HHI is at most 0.35, and all source, identity, split-normalization and decision-clock checks pass. Execution-date observability is a research assumption: any clock-ambiguous row is voided automatically. A date-cluster block bootstrap interval on aggregate replacement value must be reported descriptively; a positive result whose interval includes zero closes as a descriptive lead only and may not be labeled stable alpha.

baseline.policy: At each forward-split decision date, use the same-date cash-feasible core selected candidate if the frozen core policy admits one; otherwise retain cash for the identical horizon.

treatment.policy: For each session with at least one eligible conventional forward-split execution, select up to two active common stocks (latest as-of snapshot <= execution date, type=CS, active=true) whose split ratio satisfies the frozen conventional-ratio predicate (split_to/split_from in {n:1 for n in 2..50, 3:2, 5:4, 4:3, 5:2, 7:2} exactly), whose trailing 20 pre-event bars have >=15 rows, median dollar volume >= $1,000,000 and last close >= $3, ranked by descending median trailing dollar volume; enter the next session open, exit at the tenth subsequent session close with split-local normalization, and apply round-trip costs on a fixed $4,000 paper notional per position. Any row whose vendor classification, ratio, or decision-clock basis is shown to postdate the execution-date close is void, not re-classified.

replacement_value_comparator: The same-date cash-feasible core candidate's identical next-open-to-10-session costed value when present, otherwise zero-return cash; SPY and QQQ are reported separately and never replace the primary comparator.

execution_envelope.borrow_dependency: None; the treatment is long-only and cannot create a short.
execution_envelope.capacity_constraint: At most two selections per execution date at a fixed $4,000 paper notional each; no claim beyond research slot replacement.
execution_envelope.costs_and_carry: Use the repository round-trip cost percentage and a predeclared double-cost stress; no financing credit is assumed.
execution_envelope.intended_instrument: Cash equities exactly as identified by the Massive execution-date ticker; no ETF, option, leverage or present-day identity mapping.
execution_envelope.liquidity_dependency: Trailing 20 pre-event bars must have >=15 rows with median dollar volume >= $1,000,000 and last close >= $3; research entry requires a valid next-session open.
execution_envelope.timing_constraint: The split execution, membership and all liquidity features must be known at the execution-date New York close; entry is the next session open and exit is the fixed tenth-session close with split-local normalization.
